chapter.title: Getting Started
chapter.content: Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language. In this chapter, we cover installation, IDE setup, and your first program.

chapter.title: Variables and Types
chapter.content: Java has primitive types (int, double, boolean, char) and reference types (String, arrays, objects). We explore declarations, assignments, and type casting.

chapter.title: Control Flow
chapter.content: Learn about if-else statements, switch expressions, for loops, while loops, and how to control program execution flow.

exercise.question: What is the JVM?
exercise.answer: Java Virtual Machine - it executes Java bytecode and provides platform independence.

exercise.question: Write a Hello World program in Java.
exercise.hint: Use System.out.println inside a main method.

exercise.question: What is the difference between == and .equals() in Java?
exercise.answer: == compares references (memory addresses), while .equals() compares the actual content/values of objects.

exercise.question: Write a for loop that prints numbers 1 to 10.
exercise.hint: Use a for loop with an int counter starting at 1.
